context: Said to O'Leary, who is a fool. Daniels, who is no fool, is standing nearby and thinks he is the one addressed.
comment: What I said was true, although O'Leary, who understood what I said, and Daniels, who did not, both thought it false.

primaryText: This bar is one meter long.
context: Said by an authority fixing the reference of 'one meter' by means of a certain metal bar.
comment: The proposition expressed might have been false, although the authority could not have expressed a false proposition in that utterance.

context: Said in the actual world by a speaker who has heard three rumors about the origin of the Sherlock Holmes stories and does not know which is true.
comment: Diagonalization yields the intuitively right result: true in the actual world, false in the worlds where the name refers to someone who exists.
